text:
Ivy: Quick design review on the compact rollout scrubber: PM asked for something glanceable on tiny viewports (<=360px). Current mini-bands are losing meaning.
Marco: Agreed. At that size the 5/10/25 bands collapse. My take: introduce a 2px top border for major breakpoints (5/20/50) so users can read segmentation without relying on hue alone.
Zoe: Borders help but can still be subtle. Propose a condensed tooltip on long-press for mobile that reads e.g. 'blue variant: 10 percent, approx 8 rps' instead of forcing persistent text.
Raj: For rollback confirmation we need to avoid vague verbs. Change primary button to 'Confirm rollback to v{tag} now' and add a one-line live sparkline below showing last-minute allocations. Keeps context.
accessibility-bot: scan-result: missing aria-valuetext on scrubber handles; recommend values like 'allocation: 10 percent'. Also suggest role='application' for the scrubber only if keyboard arrow semantics are implemented.
Ivy: Keyboard: ensure left/right arrows nudge by 1%, shift+arrows by 5%, and Home/End to min/max. The focused handle needs a 3:1 contrast focus ring.
Marco: Visual note: to avoid color conflict for deuteranopia, use Okabe-Ito for variant hues and a separate alpha ramp for allocation intensity. That preserves categorical identity.
Zoe: UX microcopy: change '10%' in hover to '10 percent of traffic to canary (est. 8 req/s)' when metric is available. If unavailable show '10 percent'. Keep the width stable to avoid layout shift.
Raj: Engineering: we can provide a static estimate field for the hover and a toggle to turn it off in settings. Sparkline in modal will be a canvas with aria-hidden=true and a textual summary for screen readers.
Ivy: Action items: Marco will prototype border + condensed tooltip, Zoe will update hover copy and stable-width token, Raj will spec sparkline accessibility, and I'll update the Figma comp. Review in 36h. Thanks! :thumbsup:
